title: ID0480750-DC/Si-D/IL- [MP / P4 170000457] DC1 and DC2 Faults
description:
Reported Behavior/Issue: DC1 and DC2 Faults
Solution: Check IMD BC1
Cable Theft problem - TS2RD-68

additional_info.subject: DC1 and DC2 faults - Charger MP / P4 SN 170000457
additional_info.body:
Hello Siemens Support Team,
We would like to report faults observed on the following DC charger:
Serial number:
MP / P4 170000457
DC1 (Connector 1):
Status remains constantly in FAULTED
Log indication:
Indication: Cable theft
Visual inspection of the charging cable and socket was performed - no damage found
Insulation value measured at approximately
116 kΩ
Insulation monitoring sensor was swapped between DC1 and DC4 - same value observed (sensor is OK)
A dedicated insulation resistance test of the charging cable has not yet been performed, therefore the cable cannot be fully ruled out
DC2 (Connector 3):
Fault repeats every few minutes
Error Codes:
[OTHER_ERROR] → [NO_ERROR]
Vendor Error Code:
evse is not ready → null
Connector recovers automatically, but the fault keeps recurring
We would appreciate your guidance regarding:
The meaning and root cause of the
Cable theft
indication
Expected insulation resistance thresholds for this charger model
Recommended next diagnostic steps or known faulty components (Power Module / contactor / DC path)
Additional logs can be provided if required.
Best regards,
Ziv

additional_info.subject: ID0480750-DC/Si-D/IL- [MP / P4 170000457] DC1 and DC2 Faults CRM:03431000111
additional_info.body:
Hello Ziv, good evening.
I checked the logs and the Cable theft is being misreported. This is supposed to be sent only in case that the Cable has been cut.
I have reported this to our development team.
For the bender error, I recommend you to check by swapping BC1 and BC2 to see where the root cause lies. Don't forget to change the modbus address.
If the problem persists in BC1 (now in place of BC2) the problem is in the bender and most likely needs replacement.
If the problem is still persisting in the same position of BC1 (now BC2), then it's most likely something touching the copper bars like a loose connection or even dirt/water.
I will include the regional contact for the next steps. Please reach out to Orel if you need local support.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
